references.text: I am light and salvation; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the strength of my life; whom shall I fear? (Psalm 27:1) - Shares the direct link between God's revelation as 'I AM' and the command not to fear.

Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me (Psalm 23:4) - Connects the theme of fearlessness in dangerous surroundings (the sea/death) to God's presence.

But now thus says the Lord, who created you, O Jacob, and he who formed you, O Israel: Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine (Isaiah 43:1-2) - Uses the same combination of God's identity ('I AM' implied in the Creator) and the command 'fear not' in a situation of danger.

Fear not, for I am with you; be not dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my righteous right hand (Isaiah 41:10) - The most direct parallel to 'I AM, fear not,' where God's presence is the basis for fearlessness.
But he said to them, 'It is I; do not be afraid!' (Mark 6:50) - The direct parallel in the same miracle (Jesus walking on water), where Jesus uses the same Greek words (Egō eimi, mē phobeisthe).
